subject.title: [Bug]: Config validator rejects mediaLocalRoots despite type definitions supporting it (Telegram outbound)

question: Should OpenClaw expose configurable outbound local media roots for Telegram/media sends, and if yes should the canonical surface be broad `tools.fs.roots`, a media-specific policy, or a Telegram-only key?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix controls which host paths may be read and uploaded through channel delivery, so automation should not choose the permanent security/product boundary.

options.title: Use One Canonical Root Policy
options.body: Settle the cross-channel and filesystem-tool contract first, then implement one schema/runtime/docs/test path that covers Telegram and sibling media surfaces.

options.title: Add A Narrow Telegram Key
options.body: Expose `channels.telegram.mediaLocalRoots` only for Telegram outbound media, accepting later consolidation risk.

options.title: Keep Staged Media Only
options.body: Decline a new root config and document managed media/workspace staging as the supported security boundary.

recommendation.title: Use One Canonical Root Policy
recommendation.body: Settle the cross-channel and filesystem-tool contract first, then implement one schema/runtime/docs/test path that covers Telegram and sibling media surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent media-root and outbound access history makes this the best available routing owner for the policy choice.
